sentences.text: The operational concept covers checked baggage from acceptance at airport bag-drop or transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up, and handoff for aircraft loading.
The system boundary includes the airport equipment and control functions that convey, screen, route, reconcile, and stage checked baggage.
The boundary excludes airline aircraft loading activities beyond the handoff at the outbound load control point.
At the passenger interface, the Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit captures bag identification and accepts baggage for processing.
The Transfer Bag Feeder provides a separate induction interface for eligible transfer baggage.
The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags in a controlled manner to the screening and sorting equipment.
The Baggage Control System coordinates bag status, routing decisions, and operational visibility across connected equipment.
The Baggage Control System is also known by the alias Mosslight.
The Concourse Zone Controller coordinates local equipment and conveyance within its assigned operating area.
The Concourse Zone Controller is also known by the alias Velvet.
The Flight Data Gateway sends the Flight Cutoff Advisory.
The Baggage Control System uses current flight and operating data to support routing decisions and maintain alignment with scheduled departures.
The Concourse Zone Controller produces the Recovery Route Card.
The Primary Crossbelt Sorter routes cleared bags toward the applicable make-up areas.
The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner provide screening interfaces for baggage moving through the system.
The Image Resolution Desk supports review of screening images when automated processing requires operator assessment.
The Secondary Inspection Chute provides a controlled path for bags selected for additional examination.
The Explosives Response Team and Security Duty Manager coordinate security response and disposition for escalated screening events.
The Bag Reconciliation Station supports verification of bag identity and processing status when system records or physical handling require reconciliation.
The East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor convey routed baggage toward the relevant loading areas.
The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit supports staging of baggage for its assigned departure operation.
The Outbound Load Control Desk provides the operational interface for confirming baggage readiness at the aircraft-loading handoff.
The Airline Ramp Coordinator coordinates acceptance of staged baggage for ramp operations.
The Baggage Operations Supervisor oversees routine flow, responds to service interruptions, and coordinates operational recovery with the Security Duty Manager and Maintenance Technician.
Service objectives are to maintain safe screening, accurate bag-to-flight association, predictable throughput, and timely delivery within applicable departure cutoffs.

Equipment status, bag identity, routing state, and operating restrictions are exchanged through defined interfaces, with local staff responsible for resolving conditions that automated controls cannot clear.
